docs.title: Sales teams and the Sales groups

sections.text: Addon sales_team (depends on base and mail) is the base of every sales addon: sale and the later CRM addons depend on it, never the other way round (ADR 0199). Crate erp-addon-sales_team.

| Model | What it holds | |---|---| | crm.team | A team: name, sequence, active flag, company (empty: every company), leader (user_id), members (member_ids, crm_team_member_ids for the active memberships, crm_team_member_all_ids with the archived ones), favorites, colour. Inherits mail.thread; posting needs read access. | | crm.team.member | One membership of a user in a team, with an active flag. Archived memberships are kept. | | crm.tag | A shared label with a unique name and a colour index from 1 to 11. | | res.users (extended) | crm_team_member_ids, crm_team_ids (teams of the active memberships) and the stored sale_team_id, the team of the oldest active membership. | Company access: a team is visible in its company or everywhere when it has none; a membership follows its team (company_access = parent(edge = "crm_team_id")); a tag has no company.

- member_ids on a team is computed from the active memberships. Writing it creates the missing memberships, restores archived ones of a written user and archives the others. - An active pair of team and user exists once; a second one is refused with a validation error. - A team with a company accepts only users allowed in that company. - Unless the declared system parameter sales_team.membership_multi is true, a user has one active team: creating or restoring a membership archives the user's other active memberships. Its default is false, as in the reference; the addon reads it with erp_sdk::params::get_bool. - Archiving a user archives their memberships.

crm.team._get_default_team_id(user_id, company_id, default_team) (all Option<i64>, result Option<i64>) returns, for the user (the current user when None): a team they lead or belong to that fits company_id (teams of that company or without one), else any team of theirs, preferring default_team in both; else default_team; else the first team that fits company_id; else the first team. Only teams of the user's allowed companies or without a company count. The company and the preferred team are typed arguments, not a domain and a context key (ADR 0199 R7). Call it from another addon through the method chain: let team: Option<i64> = env .records("crm.team")? .call(tx, "_get_default_team_id", (Some(user), Some(company), current_team)) .await?;

Privilege sales_team.res_groups_privilege_sales with, from least to most access: sales_team.group_sale_salesman (own documents), sales_team.group_sale_salesman_all_leads (all documents) and sales_team.group_sale_manager (administrator, implied by base.group_system). The record rules that use them come with the documents of sale and are not shipped yet.

On install the addon creates the team "Sales" (sequence 0, no company) and makes the oldest active system administrator its leader and only member (_sales_team_seed_default_team, called from noupdate data, so it runs on install only). A database without an administrator yet keeps the team without leader. The reference's inactive Website and Point of Sale teams arrive with those applications. crm.tag ships no default records: the reference ships tags only as demo data (odoo/addons/sales_team/__manifest__.py:23-26).

List, form and search views of teams, members and tags with their window actions (sales_team.crm_team_action_config, sales_team.crm_team_member_action, sales_team.sales_team_crm_tag_action). The addon has no menu, as the reference's: the Teams entry of the Sales configuration menu belongs to sale and is not shipped yet (ADR 0199 B1).

The team dashboard (kanban and favorites on it) and the member cards are not built yet. The membership warning texts of the reference's forms, the user-picker helper fields and the activity type action are not built.
